title: Flying steampunk chair
author: Different-Director82
selftext:
Been building a Steampunk World called Copperville and I'm currently working on the Flying Steampunk Chair. What do you think about it? What improvements would you like to see? Is the sound and flying mechanics OK?

(Don't care about the rest of the world or the character, it's in it's very early development)

replies.author: SonderSoft
replies.body:
No worries at all. The idea is to use cheaper agents for various tasks. Sonnet is good at bug-finding and troubleshooting, Opus is a UI and design god (especially when you use Claude Design), and Opus is also good enough at coding. Assigning specific tasks helps immensely, and you can set the effort level of each to properly suit the task. For my setup, I have Fable give orders to an Opus middle manager so the more expensive Fable gets pinged less. 

I will admit that exclusively using Fable for coding was more reliable, but I didn't get enough done on my Max 20x plan before hitting the weekly limit; I get a lot more done each week now.

The main name of the game is to use as many tools as possible like Windows MCP, Blender MCP, and Unity MCP; for the latter, you need to subscribe to Unity's AI subscription ($10 USD/mo) to get 3 Unity MCP seats that can be used at once. As a warning, having so many Unity sessions running at once uses upwards of 55 GB of RAM. 

Best of luck. Feel free to ask any follow-up questions.

replies.author: Different-Director82
replies.body:
Fable are doing two things for me:

1) He is checking in at every iteration (when Opus has gone through each part of the game for improvements) and do a review to steer the development in the right direction.

2) Opus calls him everytime a subagent stalls/ don’t improve for a couple of rounds, to get his input.

replies.author: Material-Database-24
replies.body:
Your game has cool idea and a lot of potential. It unfortunately shows that it is likely done by AI for two reasons that seem to plague all 3d AI generated games:

- the camera is out of control 
- the model clipping/collisions bug a lot

I do not know, what's the reason, my assumption is that it's normal for hobbyist games that these are not refined and are often buggy, so the same repeats in AI generation as open source is their main training material - and open sourced old AAA games were bad at this too.

I have not yet tried doing 3d game with AI, but those two things are something AAA studios spend a lot of time with, so fixing it would be a good idea, but it may require actual understanding of the code.

So if you want to "improve" this, try get AI make the camera smoother and not go into a building, while the flying copter model clips inside the building model.

And engines like Unreal/Godot/Unity would take care of this to great degree too.
